charts.editorial_rationale: WTI crude surged from $56 in December to $98.71 by mid-March as the Strait of Hormuz crisis disrupted 20% of global oil supplies, then collapsed 34% to $83.85 after the April 17 reopening. The 46-point timeseries from October 2025 through March 15 captures the run-up from the sub-$70 breakeven zone into crisis-level pricing. The spatial relationship between the price trajectory and the $70 Alberta project breakeven threshold reveals that 42 of 46 data points in the series sat below that threshold before the crisis began -- context that prose alone cannot convey.
charts.callout_text: The project database tracks 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) with direct WTI exposure. WTI traded below the $70/bbl breakeven threshold for the entirety of October 2025 through early March 2026 before the Strait of Hormuz disruption lifted prices above $98/bbl. If ceasefire holds and WTI returns toward the $83.85 April 17 settlement, the WCS differential at $16.25/bbl would imply a WCS price near $67.60 -- below the breakeven threshold for heavy crude producers.

charts.editorial_rationale: The Government of Canada yield curve maintained its normal upward slope with a 161 basis-point spread from the 3-month tenor (2.32%) to the 30-year (3.93%) as of April 7-16. The BoC overnight rate at 2.25% anchors the short end, and the 67 basis-point 2-year to 10-year spread widened from the prior edition. The curve shape defines financing costs for 211 residential projects ($44.4B) benchmarked to the 2-year yield and 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B) exposed to the long end. A point-in-time snapshot of all 9 tenors reveals the steepness at the long end that text references cannot spatially convey.
charts.callout_text: The 30-year Government of Canada bond yield at 3.93% has risen 64 basis points year-over-year, the steepest annual increase across the six monitored tenors. The 161 basis-point spread between the 3-month yield (2.32%) and the 30-year defines the term premium that 785 power and energy projects and 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B) face when securing long-duration financing.

charts.editorial_rationale: The 2-year to 10-year Government of Canada yield spread compressed from 77 basis points on March 6 to 49 basis points on March 20 -- the tightest reading in the observation window -- as Strait of Hormuz crisis flight-to-quality flows disproportionately pushed down short-term yields. The spread subsequently recovered to 70 basis points by April 16 as the ceasefire and Strait reopening unwound crisis positioning. This 28 basis-point swing over six weeks is a spatial pattern that the narrative references but cannot convey without a chart.
charts.callout_text: The 2-year to 10-year spread compressed to 49 basis points on March 20 during peak Strait of Hormuz crisis positioning, then recovered to 70 basis points by April 16. The 28 basis-point swing reflects rate-sensitive capital repricing across 211 residential projects ($44.4B) benchmarked to the 2-year yield and 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B) exposed to long-end rates.
charts.chart_title: Government of Canada 2-Year to 10-Year Yield Spread
